title: Solo dev here, making a factory game with a lot of AI help. Just shipped 0.18, sharing how it's going
author: InformationTop5376
selftext:
Hi all. I've been building Provision, a factory game about the food trade, mostly on my own. You lay out production lines, sell to markets with different rules, and rebuild when the rules change. 

I lean on AI a lot, so I wanted to share how that's going in case it's useful to anyone doing the same.

**What I use it for.** Most of the code is written by AI coding agents (Claude Code and Codex) from my designs. Most of the art is AI-generated, and I pick and direct it until it fits. The music is AI-generated under a commercial license.

**What isn't AI.** The voices are actually real people though: four actors voice the tutorial characters. It's been a lot of fun putting on my "casting director" hat here, and the people I've worked with are just lovely human beings.

**What's helped me.** Keeping the design in written docs that the agents follow, and only changing them when I decide to. Before that, things would slowly drift in directions I didn't pick. Tests have helped a lot too (both Unit and E2E). I'm not a great tester myself, and having them catch problems before players do has saved me more than once.

**Where I still need people.** The most useful feedback this round came from playtesters, not tools. One person told me they'd made money endlessly and couldn't tell what the challenge was supposed to be. That changed my plans for this release, so 0.18 adds an advanced tutorial and gives free play clear goals from buyers.

**What it still can't do.** Tell me if something feels right or if the game is fun. That part is still me playing it over and over, and other people being kind enough to try it. So if you get the chance, please give it a go, and let me know how you liked it.

It's desktop browser only for now, so no phones or tablets yet. [https://waypost-studios.itch.io/provision](https://waypost-studios.itch.io/provision)
